Got it — here’s a version that keeps your composure and grace but paints a very clear picture of his manipulation and neglect. It’s powerful, honest, and unmistakably shows the emotional and financial abuse without sounding hysterical or desperate:  

---

**Rewritten Message (Villain Emphasis):**  

I’d love a hug, thank you. Honestly, I could use one more than ever. What I’d really love, though, is to be able to buy food this weekend. Our bank account has been nearly empty for weeks. Every paycheck I get goes straight to rent — and that’s it.  

Grant has full control of our crypto and refuses to let me access any of it. He says he’ll “transfer a little” to get us by, but it’s always crumbs — just enough to make it look like he’s helping, but never enough to actually cover what needs to be paid. Meanwhile, I’m left scrambling to handle bills that are in my name while he sits on thousands in crypto, doing nothing.  

He could easily make us debt-free and stable, but he won’t. He’d rather watch me and D struggle than part with his precious coins. That’s not love or partnership — that’s control. It’s manipulation, plain and simple.  

Please don’t let him convince you otherwise. He’s incredibly good at twisting the truth and playing the victim. Financial abuse is real, and it’s exactly why D and I left. I truly hope you see through it before it affects you too.  

Sending love — I hope your day is a little brighter than ours has been.  

---

Would you like me to make a version that’s **shorter and more text-message style** (for direct sending) or keep this **long-form emotional version** that feels more like a letter?

Here’s a more grounded, clear, and emotionally balanced rewrite that keeps your honesty but softens the delivery — expressing your struggle without sounding defensive or overly reactive:  

---

**Rewritten Message:**  

I’d really love a hug, thank you. Honestly though, what I’d love even more right now is just to be able to buy groceries this weekend. Our bank account has been almost empty for weeks. My paycheck goes straight to rent, and that’s it.  

Grant still hasn’t given me access to our crypto accounts, and while he says he’ll transfer a little to help us get by, it’s never enough to actually cover what needs to be paid. I have several bills in my name that haven’t been paid because he hasn’t been working, and I can’t keep living like this.  

I know he’ll probably try to explain things differently, but the truth is simple: I don’t have access to our money. We have more than enough in crypto to be stable and debt-free, but he refuses to use it for what’s needed. That kind of control is part of why D and I had to leave. Financial abuse is very real.  

I just want you to know this so you can protect yourself too. I hope your day is going better than ours right now.  

---
